newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler boosts Ram production at St. Louis.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler boosts Ram production at St. Louis.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Thursday it is increasing production at its St. Louis North Truck Assembly Plant by about 12,000 units per year and will start building the new Dodge Ram Quad Cab truck there starting later this summer.
Chrysler said the production increases will be fully implemented by June 3 and will allow the plant to build a total of 154,000 trucks annually.

The automaker said it has added 400 new employees at the factory in Fenton, Mo., to handle an increased assembly line speed and a new "tag relief" system, which uses a roving crew of workers to relieve individual assembly line workers during break periods. Previously the plant used a "mass relief" system in which the entire assembly line halted during breaks.

The 1998 Ram Quad Cab truck is expected to be the industry's first first full-size, extended-cab pickup to offer dual access doors to the rear seats. A Chrysler spokesman said current plans call for all of the trucks produced at the St. Louis North plant to be Quad Cab models.
Chrysler is later than its rivals in adding extra doors to its big pickup trucks but believes it can gain an edge by offering four doors instead of three.
Ford Motor Co offers a standard third door in its F-Series extended cab pickups, while General Motors Corp offers an optional third door in its extended cab Chevrolet C/K and GMC Sierra trucks.
All 1998 model Dodge Ram pickups also will offer a new instrument panel with a passenger-side air bag and a new steering wheel.
